System Design Trade-offs and Guidelines

系统设计的取舍与准则

Today’s modern technological revolution is happening because of large-scale software systems. Big enterprise companies like Google, Amazon, Oracle, and SAP have all built large-scale software systems to run their (and their customers’) businesses. Building and operating such large-scale software systems requires first-principles thinking to design and develop the technical architecture before actually putting the system into code. This is because we don’t want to be in a state where these systems will not work or scale as more users need them.

当今的技术革命之所以发生，是因为有大规模软件系统。Google、Amazon、Oracle、SAP 这样的大型企业都构建了大规模软件系统，来支撑它们自身（以及它们客户）的业务。构建并运维这样的大规模软件系统，要求在真正动手写代码之前，先用第一性原理去设计和开发技术架构。这是因为我们不希望陷入这样一种境地：随着越来越多的用户需要这些系统，它们却无法正常工作或无法扩展。

If the design is right in the first place, the rest of the implementation journey becomes smooth. This requires looking at the business requirements, understanding the needs and objectives of the customer, evaluating different trade-offs, thinking about error handling and edge cases, and contemplating future changes and robustness while worrying about basic details like algorithms and data structures. Enterprises can avoid the mistake of wasted software-development effort by carefully thinking about systems and investing time in understanding bottlenecks, system requirements, users being targeted, user access patterns, and many such decisions, which, in short, is system design.

如果一开始设计得当，后续的实现之路就会顺畅。这需要审视业务需求、理解客户的需求与目标、评估各种不同的取舍、思考错误处理与边界情况、预想未来的变化与健壮性，同时还要操心算法和数据结构这类基础细节。企业只要认真思考系统、花时间去理解瓶颈、系统需求、目标用户、用户访问模式以及诸如此类的诸多决策，就能避免软件开发精力被浪费这一错误——简而言之，这就是系统设计。

This chapter covers the basics of system design with the goal of helping you understand the fundamental concepts, the trade-offs that naturally arise in such large-scale software systems, the fallacies to avoid in building such systems, and the guidelines of system design—those lessons that have been learned from building large-scale software systems over the years. This chapter is intended to introduce you to the essentials—we’ll dig into the details in later chapters, but we want you to have a good foundation to start. Let’s begin with the basic concepts of system design.

本章介绍系统设计的基础，目标是帮助你理解基本概念、这类大规模软件系统中自然会出现的取舍、构建这类系统时要避免的谬误，以及系统设计的准则——也就是多年来从构建大规模软件系统中得到的经验教训。本章旨在向你介绍要点，我们会在后续章节中深入细节，但希望你先打好一个良好的基础。我们从系统设计的基本概念开始。

System Design Concepts

To understand the building blocks of system design, we should understand the fundamental concepts around systems. We can leverage abstraction here: the concept in computer science of obfuscating the inner details to create a model of these system design concepts, which can help us grasp the bigger picture. The concepts in system design, be it any software system, revolve around communication, consistency, availability, reliability, scalability, system maintainability, and fault tolerance. We will go over each of these concepts in detail, creating a mental model while also exploring how they are applied in large-scale system design.

要理解系统设计的积木块，我们应当理解围绕系统的基本概念。这里可以借助抽象：计算机科学中把内部细节隐藏起来、为这些系统设计概念建立模型的做法，能帮助我们把握全局。无论哪种软件系统，系统设计中的概念都围绕通信、一致性、可用性、可靠性、可扩展性、系统可维护性和容错性展开。我们将详细逐一讲解这些概念，建立心智模型，同时探讨它们在大规模系统设计中如何应用。

Communication

A large-scale software system is composed of small subsystems, known as servers, that communicate with one another—that is, they exchange information or data over the network to solve a business problem, provide business logic, and compose functionality. Communication can take place in either a synchronous or an asynchronous fashion, depending on the needs and requirements of the system. Figure 1-1 shows the differences in the sequence of actions in synchronous and asynchronous communication.

大规模软件系统由许多被称为服务器的小子系统组成，这些子系统相互通信——也就是说，它们通过网络交换信息或数据，以解决业务问题、提供业务逻辑、组合功能。通信可以是同步的，也可以是异步的，取决于系统的需要和需求。图 1-1 展示了同步通信与异步通信在动作时序上的差异。

We will cover the communication protocols as well as mechanisms for asynchronous communication in detail in Chapter 6.
我们将在第 6 章详细讲解通信协议以及异步通信的机制。
Page 28

Synchronous communication

Imagine having a phone conversation with your friend: you hear them and speak with them at the same time and use pauses in between to allow the conversation to complete. This is an example of synchronous communication: a type of communication in which two or more parties communicate with one another in real time. This type of communication is more immediate and allows for quicker resolution of issues or questions.

想象一下和朋友打电话：你同时听到对方说话、也同时和对方说话，并利用中间的停顿让对话得以完成。这就是同步通信的例子：一种两个或多个参与方实时相互通信的通信方式。这种通信更即时，能更快地解决问题或疑问。

In system design, a communication mechanism is synchronous when the sender will block (or wait) for the call or execution to return before continuing. This means that until a response is returned by the receiver, the application will not execute any further, which could be perceived by the user as latency or performance lag in the application.

在系统设计中，当发送方会阻塞（或等待）调用或执行返回之后才继续时，这种通信机制就是同步的。这意味着在接收方返回响应之前，应用程序不会再往下执行，用户可能会把这感知为应用程序的延迟或性能滞后。

Page 29

Asynchronous communication

Now, imagine that instead of a phone conversation, you switch to email. As you communicate over email with your friend, you send the message and wait for the reply to come at a later time (but within an acceptable time limit). You also follow a practice to follow up if there is no response after this time limit has passed. This is an example of asynchronous communication: a type of communication in which two or more parties do not communicate with one another in real time. Asynchronous communication can also take place through messaging platforms, forums, and social media, where users can post messages and responses may not be immediate.

现在，想象一下不是打电话，而是改用电子邮件。当你通过电子邮件和朋友交流时，你发出消息，然后在之后某个时间（但在可接受的时限内）等待回复到来。你还会养成一个习惯：如果超过这个时限还没有回复，就再跟进一下。这就是异步通信的例子：一种两个或多个参与方并不实时相互通信的通信方式。异步通信也可以通过即时通讯平台、论坛和社交媒体发生，在这些地方用户可以发布消息，而回复未必马上到来。

In system design, a communication mechanism is asynchronous when the sender does not block (or wait) for the call or execution to return from the receiver. Execution continues in your program or system, and when the call returns from the receiving server, a callback function is executed. Asynchronous communication is often used in system design when an immediate response is not required or when the system needs to be more flexible and tolerant of delays or failures.

在系统设计中，当发送方不阻塞（或不等待）接收方的调用或执行返回时，这种通信机制就是异步的。你的程序或系统继续执行，当调用从接收服务器返回时，就执行一个回调函数。当不需要即时响应、或者系统需要更灵活、更能容忍延迟或失败时，系统设计中常采用异步通信。

In general, the choice of synchronous or asynchronous communication in system design depends on the specific requirements and constraints of the system. Synchronous communication is often preferred when real-time response is needed (such as the communication between the frontend UI and the backend), while asynchronous communication is often preferred when flexibility and robustness are more important (such as checking the status of a long-running job).

总体而言，系统设计中选择同步还是异步通信，取决于系统的具体需求和约束。需要实时响应时通常更倾向同步通信（例如前端 UI 与后端之间的通信），而当灵活性和健壮性更重要时通常更倾向异步通信（例如查询一个长时间运行任务的状态）。

Consistency

Consistency—being consistent or in accordance with a set of rules or standards—is an important requirement when it comes to communication between servers in a software system. Consistency can refer to a variety of concepts and contexts in system design.

一致性——即保持一致、或符合一组规则或标准——是软件系统中服务器之间通信时的一项重要要求。在系统设计中，一致性可以指代多种不同的概念和语境。

In the context of distributed systems, consistency can be the property of all replica nodes (more on this in a moment) or servers having the same view of data at a given point in time. This means that all replica nodes have the same data, and any updates to the data are immediately reflected on all replica nodes.

在分布式系统的语境下，一致性可以指所有副本节点（稍后详述）或服务器在某一给定时刻对数据拥有相同视图的性质。这意味着所有副本节点拥有相同的数据，对数据的任何更新都会立即反映到所有副本节点上。

In the context of data storage and retrieval, consistency refers to the property of each read request returning the value of the most recent write. This means that if a write operation updates the value of a piece of data, any subsequent read requests for that data should return the updated value. Let’s discuss each of these in more detail.

在数据存储与检索的语境下，一致性指每次读请求都返回最近一次写入值的性质。这意味着如果一次写操作更新了某条数据的值，随后对该数据的任何读请求都应返回更新后的值。下面我们分别更详细地讨论。

Page 30

Consistency in distributed systems

Distributed systems are software systems that are separated physically but connected over the network to achieve common goals using shared computing resources.

分布式系统是在物理上分散、但通过网络连接起来、利用共享计算资源实现共同目标的软件系统。

Ensuring consistency—that is, providing the same view of the data to each server in a distributed system—can be challenging because multiple replica servers may be in different physical locations and may be subject to different failures or delays.

保证一致性——即在分布式系统中向每台服务器提供相同的数据视图——可能颇具挑战，因为多个副本服务器可能位于不同的物理地点，并可能遭遇不同的故障或延迟。

To address these challenges and ensure data consistency in distributed systems, we can use various techniques:

为应对这些挑战、保证分布式系统中的数据一致性，我们可以采用多种技术：

  • Data replication. In this approach, multiple copies of the data are maintained on different replica nodes, and updates to the data are made on all replica nodes simultaneously through blocking synchronous communication. This ensures that all replica nodes have the same view of the data at any given time.
    数据复制。在这种方法中，数据的多份副本被维护在不同的副本节点上，对数据的更新通过阻塞式同步通信同时在所有副本节点上进行。这保证了在任一给定时刻，所有副本节点对数据都有相同的视图。
  • Consensus protocols. Consensus protocols ensure that all replica nodes agree on the updates to be made to the data. They can use a variety of mechanisms, such as voting or leader election, to make sure all replica nodes are in agreement before updating the data.
    共识协议。共识协议确保所有副本节点就要对数据做出的更新达成一致。它们可以使用多种机制，例如投票或选主，以确保在更新数据之前所有副本节点都达成一致。
  • Conflict resolution. If two or more replica nodes try to update the same data simultaneously, conflict resolution algorithms are used to determine which update should be applied. These algorithms can employ various strategies, such as last writer wins or merge algorithms, to resolve conflicts.
    冲突解决。如果两个或更多副本节点试图同时更新同一份数据，就会使用冲突解决算法来决定应当采纳哪次更新。这些算法可以采用各种策略来解决冲突，例如最后写入胜出（last writer wins）或合并算法。

Consistency in data storage and retrieval

Large-scale software systems produce and consume a large amount of data, and thus, ensuring consistency in data storage and retrieval is important for maintaining the accuracy and integrity of the data in these systems. For example, consider a database that stores the balance of a bank account. If we withdraw money from the account, the database should reflect the updated balance immediately. If the database does not ensure consistency, it is possible for a read request to return an old balance, which could lead to incorrect financial decisions or even financial losses for us or our banks.

大规模软件系统产生并消费大量数据，因此保证数据存储与检索中的一致性，对于维持这些系统中数据的准确性和完整性非常重要。例如，考虑一个存储银行账户余额的数据库。如果我们从账户取钱，数据库应当立即反映出更新后的余额。如果数据库不保证一致性，读请求就有可能返回旧余额，这可能导致错误的财务决策，甚至给我们或我们的银行带来资金损失。

To address these challenges and ensure read consistency in data storage systems, we can use various techniques:

为应对这些挑战、保证数据存储系统中的读一致性，我们可以采用多种技术：

  • Write-ahead logging. In this technique, writes to the data are first recorded in a log before they are applied to the actual data. This ensures that if the system crashes or fails, the data can be restored to a consistent state by replaying the log.
    预写日志（Write-ahead logging）。在这种技术中，对数据的写入先记录到日志中，然后才应用到实际数据上。这保证了如果系统崩溃或发生故障，可以通过重放日志把数据恢复到一致状态。
Page 31
  • Locking. Locking mechanisms are used to ensure that only one write operation can be performed at a time. This ensures that multiple writes do not interfere with one another and that reads always return the value of the most recent write.
    加锁。加锁机制用于确保同一时刻只能执行一个写操作。这保证了多个写操作不会相互干扰，并且读操作总是返回最近一次写入的值。
  • Data versioning. In this technique, each write operation is assigned a version number, and reads always return the value of the most recent version. This allows for multiple writes to be performed concurrently while still ensuring that reads return the value of the most recent write.
    数据版本化。在这种技术中，每次写操作都会被分配一个版本号，读操作总是返回最新版本的值。这允许多个写操作并发执行，同时仍保证读操作返回最近一次写入的值。
We will discuss some of these techniques for ensuring consistency in detail in Chapters 2 and 3.
我们将在第 2 章和第 3 章详细讨论其中一些保证一致性的技术。

Consistency spectrum model

Since consistency can mean different things, the consistency spectrum model helps us reason about whether a distributed system is working correctly when it’s doing multiple things at the same time, like reading, writing, and updating data. The consistency spectrum model represents the various consistency guarantees that a distributed system can offer, ranging from eventual consistency to strong consistency. The consistency guarantee chosen depends on the specific requirements and constraints of the system. Let’s walk through the consistency levels in the consistency spectrum model:

由于一致性可以有不同含义，一致性谱系模型帮助我们推理：当分布式系统同时做多件事（例如读、写、更新数据）时，它是否在正确工作。一致性谱系模型表示分布式系统可以提供的各种一致性保证，范围从最终一致性到强一致性。选择哪种一致性保证取决于系统的具体需求和约束。下面我们逐一过一遍一致性谱系模型中的各个一致性级别：

  • Strong consistency. At one end of the spectrum, strong consistency guarantees that all replica nodes have the same view of the data at all times and that any updates to the data are immediately reflected on all replica nodes. This ensures that the data is always accurate and up to date, but it can be difficult to achieve in practice as it requires all replica nodes to be in constant communication with one another.
    强一致性。在谱系的一端，强一致性保证所有副本节点在任何时候对数据都有相同的视图，并且对数据的任何更新都会立即反映到所有副本节点上。这保证了数据始终准确、最新，但实践中可能很难达成，因为它要求所有副本节点彼此持续通信。
We will cover the strong consistency requirements of relational databases as part of the ACID model in Chapter 2.
我们将在第 2 章作为 ACID 模型的一部分，介绍关系数据库的强一致性要求。
  • Monotonic read consistency. Monotonic read consistency guarantees that once a client has read a value from a replica node, all subsequent reads from that client will return the same value or a more recent value. This means that a client will not see “stale” data that has been updated by another client.
    单调读一致性。单调读一致性保证：一旦某个客户端从某个副本节点读到了一个值，该客户端随后的所有读操作都会返回同一个值或更新的值。这意味着客户端不会看到已被另一个客户端更新过的“陈旧”数据。
    • Page 32
  • Monotonic write consistency. Monotonic write consistency guarantees that once a write operation has been acknowledged by a replica node, all subsequent reads from that replica node will return the updated value. This means that a replica node will not return outdated data to clients after a write operation has been acknowledged. This provides a stronger consistency guarantee than eventual consistency because it ensures that a replica node will not return outdated data to clients.
    单调写一致性。单调写一致性保证：一旦一次写操作已被某个副本节点确认，该副本节点随后的所有读操作都会返回更新后的值。这意味着在一次写操作被确认之后，副本节点不会再向客户端返回过时数据。它比最终一致性提供了更强的一致性保证，因为它确保副本节点不会向客户端返回过时数据。
  • Causal consistency. Causal consistency works by categorizing operations into dependent and independent operations. Dependent operations are also called causally related operations. Causal consistency preserves the order of the causally related operations. It guarantees that if two operations are causally related in dependent and independent operations, then they will be seen in the same order by all processes in the system. This means that if operation A must happen before operation B, then all processes in the system will see A before they see B. This provides a stronger consistency guarantee than eventual consistency because it ensures that the order of related operations is preserved.
    因果一致性。因果一致性的做法是把操作分为有依赖的操作和独立的操作。有依赖的操作也称为有因果关系的操作。因果一致性保留有因果关系操作的顺序。它保证：如果两个操作在有依赖和独立操作中存在因果关系，那么系统中所有进程都会按相同顺序看到它们。这意味着如果操作 A 必须发生在操作 B 之前，那么系统中所有进程看到 A 都先于看到 B。它比最终一致性提供了更强的一致性保证，因为它保证了相关操作的顺序得以保留。
  • Eventual consistency. At the other end of the spectrum, eventual consistency guarantees that, given enough time, all replica nodes will eventually have the same view of the data. This allows for more flexibility and tolerance of delays or failures but can result in temporary inconsistencies in the data.
    最终一致性。在谱系的另一端，最终一致性保证：只要给足时间，所有副本节点最终会对数据拥有相同的视图。这允许更高的灵活性、更强地容忍延迟或失败，但可能导致数据出现暂时的不一致。
We will cover the tunable consistency feature of some of the nonrelational columnar databases like Cassandra in Chapter 3.
我们将在第 3 章介绍 Cassandra 等非关系列式数据库的可调一致性特性。

Figure 1-2 shows the difference in the results of performing a sequence of actions under either strong consistency or eventual consistency. As you can see on the left showing strong consistency, when x is read from a replica node after updating it from 0 to 2, it will block the request until replication happens and then return 2 as the result. On the right illustrating eventual consistency, you can see that when the replica node is queried, it will give a stale result of x as 0 before replication completes. The consistency spectrum model therefore provides a framework for understanding the trade-offs between consistency and availability in distributed systems and helps system designers choose the appropriate consistency guarantee for their specific needs.

图 1-2 展示了在强一致性或最终一致性下执行同一串动作时结果的差异。如左图强一致性所示，把 x 从 0 更新为 2 之后再从副本节点读取 x 时，它会阻塞该请求直到复制发生，然后返回 2 作为结果。在右图最终一致性中可以看到，当查询副本节点时，它会在复制完成之前给出 x=0 的陈旧结果。因此，一致性谱系模型提供了一个框架，用于理解分布式系统中一致性与可用性之间的取舍，并帮助系统设计者为自己的特定需求选择合适的一致性保证。

Page 33

The level of consistency that a distributed system aims to achieve directly affects its complexity: stricter consistency models (like strong consistency) require extensive coordination, synchronization, and consensus across nodes, increasing latency and operational costs and making failure handling more challenging. This complexity is especially pronounced in geographically distributed systems, where network latency and scalability constraints complicate synchronization of global data. Conversely, relaxing consistency requirements (as in eventual consistency) reduces system complexity, enabling higher scalability and availability at the cost of allowing temporary data inconsistencies. Ultimately, there’s a trade-off between data accuracy and system simplicity, with each choice tailored to the specific needs and tolerance for latency, availability, and correctness in the application.

分布式系统追求达到的一致性级别直接影响其复杂度：越严格的一致性模型（例如强一致性）越需要跨节点大量的协调、同步和共识，从而增加延迟和运维成本，并让故障处理更具挑战。这种复杂度在地理分布式系统中尤为突出，网络延迟和可扩展性约束让全局数据的同步变得复杂。相反，放松一致性要求（如最终一致性）会降低系统复杂度，以允许暂时的数据不一致为代价，获得更高的可扩展性和可用性。归根结底，这是数据准确性与系统简洁性之间的权衡，每一种选择都要针对应用对延迟、可用性和正确性的具体需求与容忍度来定制。

Page 34

Availability

In a large-scale software system, subsystems or servers can go down and may not be fully available to respond to the client’s requests; this is referred to as the system’s availability. A system that is highly available can process requests and return responses in a timely manner, even under heavy load or when there are failures or errors. Let’s try to quantify the measurement of availability of the system.

在大规模软件系统中，子系统或服务器可能宕机，可能无法完全可用地响应客户端的请求；这被称为系统的可用性。一个高可用的系统即使在高负载下、或在出现故障或错误时，也能及时处理请求并返回响应。下面我们来尝试量化衡量系统的可用性。

Measuring availability

Availability can be measured mathematically as the percentage of the time the system was up (total time − time system was down) over the total time the system should have been running:

可用性在数学上可以这样衡量：系统正常运行的时间（总时间 − 系统宕机时间）占系统本应运行总时间的百分比：

Availability % = (Total Time − Sum total of downtime) / Total Time × 100

Availability percentages are represented in nines based on this formula over a period of time. You can see a breakdown of what these numbers really work out to in Table 1-1.

根据这个公式，在一段时间内，可用性百分比用“几个 9”来表示。这些数字实际意味着什么，可以在表 1-1 中看到详细分解。

Availability percentageDowntime per yearDowntime per monthDowntime per week
90% (1 nine)36.5 days72 hours16.8 hours
99% (2 nines)3.65 days7.2 hours1.68 hours
99.5% (2 nines)1.83 days3.60 hours50.4 minutes
99.9% (3 nines)8.76 hours43.8 minutes10.1 minutes
99.99% (4 nines)52.56 minutes4.32 minutes1.01 minutes
99.999% (5 nines)5.26 minutes25.9 seconds6.05 seconds
99.9999% (6 nines)31.5 seconds2.59 seconds0.605 seconds
99.99999% (7 nines)3.15 seconds0.259 seconds0.0605 seconds

表 1-1　用“几个 9”表示的可用性百分比（对应的每年/每月/每周停机时间）。

The goal for availability usually is to achieve the highest level possible, such as “five nines” (99.999%) or even “six nines” (99.9999%). However, the level of availability that is considered realistic or achievable depends on several factors, including the complexity of the system, the resources available for maintenance and redundancy, and the specific requirements of the application or service.

可用性的目标通常是达到尽可能高的级别，例如“五个 9”（99.999%）甚至“六个 9”（99.9999%）。然而，被认为现实或可达成的可用性级别取决于多个因素，包括系统的复杂度、可用于维护和冗余的资源，以及应用或服务的具体需求。

Page 35

Achieving higher levels of availability becomes progressively more challenging and resource intensive. Each additional nine requires an exponential increase in redundancy, fault-tolerant architecture, and rigorous maintenance practices. It often involves implementing redundant components, backup systems, load balancing, failover mechanisms, and continuous monitoring to minimize downtime and ensure rapid recovery in case of failures.

达到更高的可用性级别会逐渐变得更具挑战、更耗费资源。每多一个 9，都需要在冗余、容错架构和严格运维实践上呈指数级增长。这通常涉及实现冗余组件、备份系统、负载均衡、故障转移机制以及持续监控，以最小化停机时间，并确保在发生故障时能快速恢复。

While some critical systems, such as financial trading platforms or emergency services, may strive for the highest levels of availability, achieving and maintaining them can be extremely difficult and costly. In contrast, for less critical applications or services with a lower level of availability, such as 99% or 99.9%, may be more realistic and achievable within reasonable resource constraints.

虽然某些关键系统（例如金融交易平台或应急服务）可能会追求最高级别的可用性，但达成并维持这些级别可能极其困难且代价高昂。相反，对于不那么关键的应用或服务，较低的可用性级别（例如 99% 或 99.9%）在合理的资源约束下可能更现实、更可达成。

Ultimately, determining what level of availability is realistic and achievable depends on a careful evaluation of the specific requirements, resources, costs, and trade-offs involved in each case.

归根结底，确定什么级别的可用性是现实且可达成的，需要仔细评估每种情况下涉及的具体需求、资源、成本和取舍。

Availability in parallel versus in sequence

The availability of a system that consists of multiple subsystems depends on whether the components are arranged in sequence or in parallel with respect to serving the request. Figure 1-3 shows the arrangement of components in the sequential system on the left, where the request needs to be served from each component in sequence, and the parallel system on the right, where the request can be served from either component in parallel.

由多个子系统组成的系统，其可用性取决于这些组件在服务请求时是串联还是并联排列。图 1-3 左侧展示了串联系统中组件的排列方式，请求需要依次由每个组件来服务；右侧展示了并联系统，请求可以由任一组件并行地服务。

Page 36

If the components are in sequence, the overall availability of the service will be the product of the availability of each component. For example, if two components with 99.9% availability are in sequence, their total availability will be 99.8%:

如果组件是串联的，服务的整体可用性将是每个组件可用性的乘积。例如，如果两个可用性为 99.9% 的组件串联，它们的总可用性将为 99.8%：

Availability of two components in sequence
  = Availability of component 1 × Availability of component 2
  = 0.999 × 0.999 = 0.998001 ≈ 99.8%

On the other hand, if the components are in parallel, the overall availability of the service will be the sum of the availability of each component minus the product of their unavailability. For example, if two components with 99.9% availability are in parallel, their total availability will be 99.9999%. This can lead to significantly higher availability compared to the same components arranged in sequence (from 3 nines to 6 nines in the example):

另一方面，如果组件是并联的，服务的整体可用性将是每个组件可用性之和减去它们不可用性的乘积。例如，如果两个可用性为 99.9% 的组件并联，它们的总可用性将为 99.9999%。与同样这些组件串联相比，这能带来显著更高的可用性（在本例中从三个 9 提升到六个 9）：

Availability of two components in parallel
  = 1 − Unavailability of both components
  = 1 − P(component 1 going down) × P(component 2 going down)
  = 1 − 0.001 × 0.001 = 1 − 0.000001
  = 0.999999 ≈ 99.9999%

The arrangement of components in a service can have a significant impact on its overall availability, so it is important to consider this when designing a system for high availability.

服务中组件的排列方式会对其整体可用性产生重大影响，因此在为高可用设计系统时考虑这一点非常重要。

Ensuring availability

Ensuring availability in a system is critical for maintaining the performance and reliability of the system. There are several ways to increase the availability of a system:

在系统中保证可用性，对于维持系统的性能和可靠性至关重要。有几种方法可以提高系统的可用性：

  • Redundancy. When a system has multiple copies of critical components or subsystems, it can continue to function even if one component fails. This can be achieved by using redundant load balancers, failover systems, or replicated data stores.
    冗余。当一个系统拥有关键组件或子系统的多份副本时，即使某个组件发生故障，它也能继续运行。这可以通过使用冗余负载均衡器、故障转移系统或复制的数据存储来实现。
  • Fault tolerance. Systems designed to be resistant to failures or errors can continue to function even when there are unexpected events. This can be achieved by using error-handling mechanisms, redundant hardware, or self-healing systems.
    容错。被设计为对故障或错误有抵抗力的系统，即使在出现意外事件时也能继续运行。这可以通过使用错误处理机制、冗余硬件或自愈系统来实现。
  • Load balancing. By distributing incoming requests among multiple servers or components, a system can more effectively handle heavy loads and maintain high availability. This can be achieved by using multiple load balancers or distributed systems.
    负载均衡。通过把进来的请求分发到多台服务器或组件上，系统可以更有效地处理高负载并维持高可用性。这可以通过使用多个负载均衡器或分布式系统来实现。
We will cover load balancing in detail in Chapter 5 and explore the different types of AWS load balancers in Chapter 9.
我们将在第 5 章详细讲解负载均衡，并在第 9 章探讨 AWS 负载均衡器的不同类型。
Page 37

Availability patterns

There are two major complementary patterns to support high availability: failover and replication.

支撑高可用主要有两种互补的模式：故障转移（failover）和复制（replication）。

Failover patterns. Failover refers to the process of switching to a redundant or backup system in the event of a failure or error in the primary system. The failover pattern chosen depends on the specific requirements and constraints of the system, including the desired level of availability and the cost of implementing the failover solution. The two main types of failover patterns are active-active and active-passive:

故障转移模式。故障转移指在主系统发生故障或错误时，切换到冗余或备份系统的过程。选择哪种故障转移模式取决于系统的具体需求和约束，包括期望的可用性级别以及实现故障转移方案的成本。故障转移模式主要有两种：主主（active-active）和主备（active-passive）：

  • Active-active failover. In an active-active failover pattern, as shown on the left in Figure 1-4, multiple systems are used in parallel, and all systems are actively processing requests. If one system fails, the remaining systems can continue to process requests and maintain high availability. This approach allows for more flexibility and better utilization of resources but can be more complex to implement and maintain because it requires more sophisticated load balancing and failover mechanisms.
    主主故障转移。在主主故障转移模式中，如图 1-4 左侧所示，多套系统并行使用，所有系统都在主动处理请求。如果一套系统发生故障，其余系统可以继续处理请求并维持高可用性。这种方式允许更高的灵活性和更好的资源利用率，但实现和维护可能更复杂，因为它需要更成熟的负载均衡和故障转移机制。
  • Active-passive failover. In an active-passive failover pattern, as shown on the right in Figure 1-4, one system is designated as the primary system and actively processes requests while one or more backup systems are maintained in a passive state. If the primary system fails, the backup system is activated to take over processing of requests. This approach is simpler to implement and maintain because data only needs to be replicated in one direction: from the active server to the passive server. It also avoids the complexities of data conflicts and the synchronization issues that can occur in an active-active setup. However, this can result in reduced availability if the primary system fails, as there is a delay in switching to the backup system.
    主备故障转移。在主备故障转移模式中，如图 1-4 右侧所示，一套系统被指定为主系统、主动处理请求，同时一套或多套备份系统维持在被动状态。如果主系统发生故障，备份系统会被激活以接管请求处理。这种方式实现和维护更简单，因为数据只需在一个方向上复制：从活动服务器到被动服务器。它还避免了主主配置中可能出现的数据冲突复杂性和同步问题。然而，如果主系统发生故障，由于切换到备份系统存在延迟，这可能导致可用性下降。

Failover patterns can require additional hardware and can add complexity to the system. There is also the potential for data loss if the active system fails before newly written data can be replicated to the passive system. The choice of failover pattern depends on the specific requirements and constraints of the system, including the desired level of availability and the cost of implementing the failover solution.

故障转移模式可能需要额外的硬件，并会增加系统的复杂性。此外，如果活动系统在新写入的数据还未复制到被动系统之前就发生故障，还有可能丢失数据。选择哪种故障转移模式取决于系统的具体需求和约束，包括期望的可用性级别以及实现故障转移方案的成本。

These failover patterns are employed in relational data stores, nonrelational data stores, caches, and load balancers, which we will cover in Chapters 2, 3, 4, and 5, respectively.
这些故障转移模式应用于关系数据存储、非关系数据存储、缓存和负载均衡器，我们将分别在第 2、3、4、5 章讲解。
Page 38

Replication patterns. Replication is the process of maintaining multiple copies of data or other resources to improve availability and fault tolerance. The replication pattern chosen depends on the specific requirements and constraints of the system, including the desired level of availability and the cost of implementing the replication solution. The two main types of replication patterns are multileader and single leader:

复制模式。复制是维护数据或其他资源的多份副本、以提高可用性和容错性的过程。选择哪种复制模式取决于系统的具体需求和约束，包括期望的可用性级别以及实现复制方案的成本。复制模式主要有两种：多主（multileader）和单主（single leader）：

  • Multileader replication. In a multileader replication pattern, as shown on the left in Figure 1-5, multiple systems are used in parallel, and all systems can read and write data. This allows for more flexibility and better utilization of resources because all systems can process requests and updates to the data simultaneously. A load balancer is required or application logic changes need to be made to support multiple leaders and identify on which leader node to write. Most multileader systems either are loosely consistent or have increased write latency for synchronization to remain consistent. Conflict resolution comes more into play as more write nodes are added, leading to increases in latency. This approach can become complex to implement and maintain because it requires careful management of conflicts and errors.
    多主复制。在多主复制模式中，如图 1-5 左侧所示，多套系统并行使用，所有系统都可以读写数据。这允许更高的灵活性和更好的资源利用率，因为所有系统都可以同时处理请求和对数据的更新。需要一个负载均衡器，或者需要修改应用逻辑，以支持多个主节点并识别应当往哪个主节点写入。大多数多主系统要么是松散一致的，要么为了保持一致而提高了写延迟。随着加入更多写入节点，冲突解决变得更加重要，从而导致延迟增加。这种方式的实现和维护可能变得复杂，因为需要仔细管理冲突和错误。
  • Single-leader replication. In a single-leader replication pattern, as shown on the right in Figure 1-5, one system is designated as the leader system and is responsible for both reading and writing data while one or more follower systems are used to replicate the data. The follower systems can be used only for reading data; updates to the data must be made on the leader system. Additional logic is required to be implemented to promote a follower to the leader. This approach is simpler to implement and
    单主复制。在单主复制模式中，如图 1-5 右侧所示，一套系统被指定为主系统，负责读写数据，同时一套或多套从系统用于复制数据。从系统只能用于读取数据；对数据的更新必须在主系统上进行。需要实现额外的逻辑来把从节点提升为主节点。这种方式实现和维护更简单，
Page 39

maintain but can result in reduced availability if the leader system fails because updates to the data can be made only on the leader system and there is a risk of losing the data updates.

但如果主系统发生故障，可能导致可用性下降，因为对数据的更新只能在主系统上进行，并且存在丢失数据更新的风险。

There is a risk of data loss if the leader system fails before newly written data can be replicated to other nodes. The more read replicas that are used, the more writes need to be replicated, which can lead to greater replication lag. In addition, using read replicas can affect the performance of the system because the system may get bogged down with replaying writes and become unable to process as many reads. Furthermore, replication can require additional hardware that can add complexity to the system. Finally, some systems may have more efficient write performance on the leader system since it can spawn multiple threads to write in parallel, while read replicas may only support writing sequentially with a single thread. The choice of replication pattern depends on the specific requirements and constraints of the system, including the desired level of availability and the cost of implementing the replication solution.

如果主系统在新写入的数据还未复制到其他节点之前就发生故障，就有数据丢失的风险。使用的读副本越多，需要复制的写操作就越多，这可能导致更大的复制延迟。此外，使用读副本可能影响系统性能，因为系统可能会被回放写操作拖慢，从而无法处理同样多的读请求。而且，复制可能需要额外的硬件，这会增加系统的复杂性。最后，某些系统在主系统上的写性能可能更高，因为它可以派生多个线程并行写入，而读副本可能只支持单线程顺序写入。选择哪种复制模式取决于系统的具体需求和约束，包括期望的可用性级别以及实现复制方案的成本。

We will cover how relational and nonrelational data stores ensure availability using single-leader and multileader replication in Chapters 2 and 3. Do look out for leaderless replication using consistent hashing to ensure availability in nonrelational stores like key-value stores and columnar stores in Chapter 3.
我们将在第 2 章和第 3 章讲解关系与非关系数据存储如何用单主和多主复制保证可用性。请留意第 3 章中键值存储、列式存储等非关系存储里用一致性哈希实现无主复制来保证可用性的内容。
Page 40

Reliability

In system design, reliability refers to the ability of a system or component to perform its intended function consistently and without failure over a given period of time. It is a measure of the dependability or trustworthiness of the system. Reliability is typically expressed as a probability or percentage of time that the system will operate without failure. For example, a system with a reliability of 99% will fail only 1% of the time. Let’s try to quantify the measurement of reliability of the system.

在系统设计中，可靠性指一个系统或组件在给定时间段内持续、无故障地完成其既定功能的能力。它是对系统可依赖性或可信赖程度的度量。可靠性通常用系统无故障运行的概率或时间百分比来表示。例如，一个可靠性为 99% 的系统只有 1% 的时间会发生故障。下面我们来尝试量化衡量系统的可靠性。

Measuring reliability

One way to measure the reliability of a system is by using mean time between failures (MTBF) and mean time to repair (MTTR).

衡量系统可靠性的一种方法是使用平均无故障时间（MTBF）和平均修复时间（MTTR）。

Mean time between failures. MTBF is a measure of the average amount of time that a system can operate without experiencing a failure. It is typically expressed in hours or other units of time. The higher the MTBF, the more reliable the system is considered to be:

平均无故障时间。MTBF 衡量系统在不发生故障的情况下平均可运行的时间。它通常以小时或其他时间单位表示。MTBF 越高，系统被认为越可靠：

Mean time between failures (MTBF)
  = (Total Elapsed Time − Sum total of downtime) / Total Number of Failures

For mission-critical systems, an MTBF of tens of thousands of hours or more is generally desired, while consumer electronics may have lower MTBF values. For example, high-reliability servers typically aim for an MTBF of 50,000 hours or more; consumer-grade laptops may have an MTBF of around 5,000−10,000 hours. MTBF helps estimate the frequency of failures, allowing for better planning and budgeting of maintenance activities. If MTBF is low for a critical component, redundancy can be implemented to minimize downtime. In high-availability setups, multiple servers or components with lower MTBFs may be clustered to achieve overall reliability. As MTBF increases with design changes, you can quantitatively assess reliability improvements, ultimately leading to fewer failures and reduced operational costs.

对于关键任务系统，通常希望 MTBF 达到数万小时或更高，而消费类电子产品的 MTBF 可能较低。例如，高可靠服务器通常以 MTBF 5 万小时或更高为目标；消费级笔记本电脑的 MTBF 可能在 5000～10000 小时左右。MTBF 有助于估计故障发生的频率，从而更好地规划和安排维护活动的预算。如果某个关键组件的 MTBF 较低，可以通过实现冗余来最小化停机时间。在高可用配置中，可以把多台 MTBF 较低的服务器或组件组成集群，以获得整体的可靠性。随着设计变更使 MTBF 提高，你可以定量评估可靠性的提升，最终带来更少的故障和更低的运维成本。

Page 41

Mean time to repair. MTTR is a measure of the average amount of time it takes to repair a failure in the system. It is also typically expressed in hours or other units of time. The lower the MTTR, the more quickly the system can be restored to operation after a failure:

平均修复时间。MTTR 衡量修复系统中一次故障平均所需的时间。它通常也以小时或其他时间单位表示。MTTR 越低，系统在故障后就能越快恢复运行：

Mean time to repair (MTTR) = Total Maintenance Time / Total Number of Repairs

Together, MTBF and MTTR can be used to understand the overall reliability of a system. For example, a system with a high MTBF and a low MTTR is considered to be more reliable than a system with a low MTBF and a high MTTR as it is less likely to experience failures and can be restored to operation more quickly when failures do occur.

MTBF 和 MTTR 合在一起，可以用来理解系统的整体可靠性。例如，一个 MTBF 高、MTTR 低的系统，被认为比 MTBF 低、MTTR 高的系统更可靠，因为它发生故障的可能性更小，而且在故障确实发生时能更快恢复运行。

Reliability and availability

It is important to note that reliability and availability are not mutually exclusive. A system can be both reliable and available, or it can be neither. A system that is reliable but not available is not particularly useful since it may be reliable but not able to perform its intended function when needed. A system that is available but not reliable is also not useful since it may be able to perform its intended function when needed, but it may not do so consistently or without failure.

需要注意的是，可靠性和可用性并不是互斥的。一个系统可以既可靠又可用，也可以两者都不具备。一个可靠但不可用的系统没什么用，因为它可能可靠，但在需要时无法执行其既定功能。一个可用但不可靠的系统同样没用，因为它可能在需要时能执行既定功能，却无法持续地、无故障地做到。

To achieve high reliability and availability to meet agreed service-level objectives (SLOs), it is important to design and maintain systems with redundant components and robust failover mechanisms. Performing maintenance and testing regularly also ensures that the system is operating at its optimal level of performance. In general, the reliability of a system is an important consideration in system design because it can affect the performance and availability of the system over time.

为达到高可靠性和高可用性、满足约定的服务水平目标（SLO），重要的是用冗余组件和健壮的故障转移机制来设计和维护系统。定期进行维护和测试也能确保系统运行在最佳性能水平。总体而言，系统的可靠性是系统设计中一项重要的考量，因为它会随时间影响系统的性能和可用性。

SLOs and goals, including change management, problem management, and service request management, of AWS Managed Services (introduced in Part II) are provided in the AWS documentation.
AWS 托管服务（将在第二部分介绍）的 SLO 与目标（包括变更管理、问题管理和服务请求管理）见 AWS 文档。

Scalability

Page 42

In system design, we need to ensure that the performance of the system increases with the resources added based on the increasing workload, which can be either request workload or data storage workload. This is referred to as scalability in system design, which requires the system to respond to increased demand and load. For example, a social network needs to scale with the increasing number of users as well as the content feed on the platform that it indexes and serves.

在系统设计中，我们需要确保系统性能随着为应对不断增长的工作负载而加入的资源一同提升，这里的工作负载可以是请求负载，也可以是数据存储负载。这在系统设计中称为可扩展性，它要求系统能够响应增长的需求和负载。例如，一个社交网络需要随着用户数的增长、以及它所索引和分发的平台上内容 feed 的增长而扩展。

The two major complementary patterns to scale a system are vertical scaling and horizontal scaling:

扩展系统主要有两种互补模式：垂直扩展和水平扩展：

  • Vertical scaling. Vertical scaling involves meeting the load requirements of the system by increasing the capacity of a single server by upgrading it with more resources (CPU, RAM, graphics processing units, storage, etc.), as shown on the left in Figure 1-6. Vertical scaling is useful when dealing with predictable traffic since it allows for more resources to be used to handle the existing demand. However, there are limitations to how much a single server can scale up based on its current configuration. The cost of scaling up is also generally high as adding more higher-end resources to the existing server will require a greater investment.
    垂直扩展。垂直扩展指通过给单台服务器升级更多资源（CPU、内存、图形处理器、存储等）来提升其容量，从而满足系统的负载需求，如图 1-6 左侧所示。垂直扩展在应对可预测流量时很有用，因为它允许用更多资源来处理已有需求。然而，单台服务器基于其当前配置能纵向扩展的幅度是有限的。纵向扩展的成本通常也较高，因为给现有服务器加装更多高端资源需要更大的投入。
  • Horizontal scaling. Horizontal scaling involves meeting the load requirements of the system by increasing the number of the servers by adding more commodity servers to serve the requests, as shown on the right in Figure 1-6. Horizontal scaling is useful when dealing with unpredictable traffic because there is increased capacity to handle more requests, and if demand arises, more servers can be added to the pool cost-effectively. Although horizontal scaling provides a better cost proposition for scaling, the complexity of managing multiple servers and ensuring that they work collectively as an abstracted single server to handle the workload is the catch here.
    水平扩展。水平扩展指通过增加服务器数量、加入更多通用服务器来服务请求，从而满足系统的负载需求，如图 1-6 右侧所示。水平扩展在应对不可预测流量时很有用，因为有了更大的容量来处理更多请求；如果需求上升，还可以高性价比地向资源池中加入更多服务器。虽然水平扩展在扩展成本上更划算，但难点在于管理多台服务器、并确保它们像一台抽象出来的单机那样协同工作来处理工作负载。
We will cover both scaling approaches and mechanisms in detail in Chapter 5.
我们将在第 5 章详细讲解这两种扩展方式和机制。

In early-stage systems, you can start scaling up by vertically scaling the system and adding better configurations to it. Later, when you hit the limitation in scaling up, you can move to horizontally scaling the system.

在早期系统中，你可以先从垂直扩展入手，给系统加更好的配置。之后，当碰到纵向扩展的上限时，再转向水平扩展。

Maintainability

In system design, maintainability is the system’s ability to be modified, adapted, or extended to meet the changing needs of its users while ensuring smooth operations. For a software system to be maintainable, it must be designed to be flexible and easy to modify or extend. Maintainability involves these three underlying aspects of the system:

在系统设计中，可维护性指系统在保证平稳运行的同时，能够被修改、适配或扩展以满足用户不断变化的需求的能力。一个软件系统要具备可维护性，就必须被设计得灵活、易于修改或扩展。可维护性涉及系统以下三个内在方面：

Page 43
  • Operability. This requires the system to operate smoothly under normal conditions and even return to normal operations within a stipulated time after a fault. When a system is maintainable in terms of operability, that reduces the time and effort required to keep the system running smoothly. This is important because efficient operations and management contribute to overall system stability, reliability, and availability.
    可操作性。这要求系统在正常条件下平稳运行，甚至在发生故障后能在规定时间内恢复正常运行。当一个系统在可操作性方面可维护时，就能减少让系统平稳运行所需的时间和精力。这很重要，因为高效的运维和管理有助于整体系统的稳定性、可靠性和可用性。
  • Lucidity. This requires the system to be simple and clear to understand, to extend by adding features, and even to fix bugs. When a system is lucid, that enables efficient collaboration among team members, simplifies debugging and maintenance tasks, and facilitates knowledge transfer. It also reduces the risk of introducing errors during modifications or updates.
    清晰性。这要求系统简单清晰、易于理解、易于通过加功能来扩展，甚至易于修 bug。当一个系统清晰时，就能让团队成员高效协作，简化调试和维护工作，并便于知识传递。它还能降低在修改或更新过程中引入错误的风险。
  • Modifiability. This requires the system to be built in a modular way to allow it to be changed and extended easily, without disrupting the functionality of other subsystems. Modifiability is vital because software systems need to evolve to adapt to new business needs, technological advancements, or user feedback. A system that lacks modifiability can become stagnant, resistant to change, and difficult to enhance or adapt to future demands.
    可修改性。这要求系统以模块化方式构建，使其能够被轻松地修改和扩展，而不破坏其他子系统的功能。可修改性至关重要，因为软件系统需要演进，以适应新的业务需求、技术进步或用户反馈。一个缺乏可修改性的系统会变得停滞、抗拒变化，难以增强或适应未来的需求。

By prioritizing maintainability, organizations can reduce downtime, lower maintenance costs, enhance productivity, and increase the longevity and value of their software systems.

通过把可维护性放在优先位置，组织可以减少停机时间、降低维护成本、提升生产率，并延长其软件系统的寿命和价值。

Fault Tolerance

Large-scale systems generally employ a large number of servers and storage devices to handle and respond to user requests and store data. Fault tolerance requires the system to recover from any failure (either hardware or software failure) and continue to serve the requests. This means avoiding single points of failure in a large system and being able to reroute requests to functioning subsystems to complete the workload. Fault tolerance needs to be supported at hardware as well as software levels while ensuring data safety—that is, making sure the data is not lost. The two major mechanisms to ensure data safety are replication and checkpointing.

大规模系统通常使用大量服务器和存储设备来处理和响应用户请求、存储数据。容错性要求系统能够从任何故障（硬件或软件故障）中恢复，并继续服务请求。这意味着要避免大型系统中的单点故障，并能够把请求重新路由到正常运行的子系统来完成工作负载。容错需要在硬件和软件两层都得到支持，同时还要保证数据安全——也就是确保数据不丢失。保证数据安全的两大主要机制是复制和检查点（checkpointing）。

  • Replication. Replication-based fault tolerance ensures both data safety and serving the request by replicating the service through multiple replica servers and replicating the data as multiple copies across multiple storage servers. During a failure, the failed node is swapped with a fully functioning replica node. Similarly, data is served again from a replica store in case the data store has failed. We discussed replication patterns in “Availability” on page 13.
    复制。基于复制的容错通过把服务复制到多台副本服务器上、把数据复制为多份副本分散到多台存储服务器上，同时保证数据安全和请求服务。在发生故障时，故障节点被替换为一个完全正常运行的副本节点。同样，如果数据存储发生故障，就从副本存储重新提供数据。我们已在第 13 页“可用性”一节讨论过复制模式。
    • Page 44
  • Checkpointing. Checkpointing-based fault tolerance ensures that data is reliably stored and backed up, even after the initial processing is completed. It allows for a system to recover from any potential data loss by restoring a previous system state and preventing data loss. Checkpointing is commonly used to ensure system and data integrity, especially when dealing with large datasets. It can also be used to verify that data is not corrupted or missing because it can quickly detect any changes or issues in the data and then take corrective measures. Checkpointing is an important tool for data integrity, reliability, and security.
    检查点。基于检查点的容错确保即使在初始处理完成之后，数据也被可靠地存储和备份。它让系统能够通过恢复之前的系统状态来从任何潜在的数据丢失中恢复、防止数据丢失。检查点常用于保证系统和数据的完整性，尤其是在处理大型数据集时。它还可用于验证数据没有损坏或缺失，因为它能快速检测数据中的任何变化或问题，然后采取纠正措施。检查点是保障数据完整性、可靠性和安全性的重要工具。
Recovery managers of databases use checkpointing to ensure the durability and reliability of the database in the event of failures or crashes. This will be covered in detail in Chapter 2.
数据库的恢复管理器利用检查点来保证数据库在故障或崩溃情况下的持久性和可靠性。这将在第 2 章详细讲解。

Checkpointing can be done using either synchronous or asynchronous mechanisms:

检查点可以用同步机制，也可以用异步机制来完成：

  • Synchronous checkpointing. Synchronous checkpointing in a system is achieved by stopping all the data mutation requests and allowing only read requests while waiting for the checkpointing process to complete for the current data mutation. This always ensures a consistent data state across all the nodes.
    同步检查点。系统中的同步检查点是通过停止所有数据变更请求、只允许读请求来实现的，同时等待当前数据变更的检查点过程完成。这始终能保证所有节点之间的数据状态一致。
  • Asynchronous checkpointing. Asynchronous checkpointing in a system is done by checkpointing asynchronously on all the nodes while continuing to serve all the requests (including data mutation requests) without waiting for the acknowledgment of the checkpointing process to complete. This mechanism suffers from the possibility of having an inconsistent data state across the servers.
    异步检查点。系统中的异步检查点是在所有节点上异步地做检查点，同时继续服务所有请求（包括数据变更请求），而不等待检查点过程完成的确认。这种机制的问题在于，各服务器之间可能出现数据状态不一致。

In checkpointing-based fault tolerance, recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) are key metrics that help define the effectiveness of data recovery and system reliability:

在基于检查点的容错中，恢复时间目标（RTO）和恢复点目标（RPO）是帮助定义数据恢复有效性和系统可靠性的关键指标：

  • Recovery point objective. RPO defines the maximum acceptable amount of data loss measured in time. It represents how much data a system can afford to lose before that significantly affects operations. In checkpointing, RPO determines how frequently checkpoints should be created. For instance, if the RPO is set to 15 minutes, the system should take a checkpoint every 15 minutes to ensure that no more than
    恢复点目标。RPO 以时间衡量，定义可接受的最大数据丢失量。它表示系统在数据丢失严重影响运行之前，能承受丢失多少数据。在检查点中，RPO 决定应当多久创建一次检查点。例如，如果 RPO 设为 15 分钟，系统就应每 15 分钟做一次检查点，以保证恢复时丢失的数据不超过
    • Page 45
  • 15 minutes’ worth of data is lost during recovery. A smaller RPO (more frequent checkpoints) provides better data protection but can increase system load and storage requirements. For large datasets, achieving a low RPO requires efficient data storage and fast checkpointing.
    15 分钟。更小的 RPO（更频繁的检查点）能提供更好的数据保护，但会增加系统负载和存储需求。对于大型数据集，要实现低 RPO 需要高效的数据存储和快速的检查点。
  • Recovery time objective. RTO specifies the maximum acceptable downtime following a failure, indicating how quickly the system should be restored to operational status. Checkpointing helps reduce RTO by allowing the system to resume from the most recent checkpoint rather than restarting from scratch. Faster recovery time is critical when handling large datasets or processing real-time data, where any downtime can impact users or services. The effectiveness of checkpointing on RTO depends on the ease of restoring data from the checkpoint and the system’s ability to resume operations quickly without extensive reprocessing.
    恢复时间目标。RTO 规定故障后可接受的最大停机时间，表明系统应当多快恢复到运行状态。检查点通过让系统从最近的检查点恢复、而不是从零重启，来帮助降低 RTO。在处理大型数据集或实时数据时，更快的恢复时间至关重要，因为任何停机都可能影响用户或服务。检查点对 RTO 的效果，取决于从检查点恢复数据的难易程度，以及系统无需大量重新处理即可快速恢复运行的能力。

You should now understand the basic concepts and requirements of a large-scale system. We strive toward building a performant and scalable system—one that is also highly available, reliable, maintainable, and fault tolerant. Before getting into how to build such systems, let’s go through the inherent fallacies as well as the trade-offs in designing them.

现在你应当已经理解了大规模系统的基本概念和要求。我们努力构建一个高性能、可扩展的系统——同时它还要高可用、可靠、可维护、可容错。在讲如何构建这类系统之前，我们先来过一下设计这类系统时固有的谬误和取舍。

Fallacies of Distributed Computing

Because a large-scale software system involves multiple distributed systems, it is often subject to certain fallacies that can lead to incorrect assumptions and implementations. These fallacies were introduced by L. Peter Deutsch. They cover the false assumptions that software developers commonly make when implementing distributed systems. The eight fallacies are as follows:

由于大规模软件系统涉及多个分布式系统，它常常会陷入某些谬误，导致错误的假设和实现。这些谬误由 L. Peter Deutsch 提出。它们涵盖了软件开发者在实现分布式系统时通常会做出的错误假设。这八条谬误如下：

  • Reliable network. The first fallacy is assuming that “the network is reliable.” Networks are complex, dynamic, and often unpredictable. Small issues like switch or power failures can bring the entire network of a data center down, making the network unreliable. Thus, it is important to account for the potential of an unreliable network when designing large-scale systems, ensuring network fault tolerance from the start. Given that networks are inherently unreliable, to build reliable services on top we must rely on protocols that can cope with network outages and packet loss.
    可靠的网络。第一条谬误是假设“网络是可靠的”。网络复杂、动态、往往不可预测。交换机故障或供电故障这类小问题就可能让一个数据中心的整个网络瘫痪，使网络变得不可靠。因此，在设计大规模系统时，必须考虑到网络可能不可靠，从一开始就保证网络容错。鉴于网络本质上不可靠，要在其上构建可靠的服务，我们必须依赖能够应对网络中断和丢包的协议。
  • Zero latency. The second fallacy is assuming that “latency is zero.” Latency is an inherent limitation of networks, constrained by the speed of light—that is, even in theoretically perfect systems, the data can’t transfer between the nodes faster than the speed of light. To account for latency, the system should be designed to bring clients close to the data through edge computing and even by choosing the
    零延迟。第二条谬误是假设“延迟为零”。延迟是网络固有的局限，受光速约束——也就是说，即使在理论上完美的系统中，数据在节点间传输也不可能快过光速。为应对延迟，系统应被设计为通过边缘计算让客户端靠近数据，甚至通过选择
    • Page 46
  • servers in geographic data centers nearer to the clients and routing the traffic wisely.
    位于离客户端更近的地理数据中心中的服务器，并明智地路由流量。
  • Infinite bandwidth. The third fallacy is assuming that “bandwidth is infinite.” When a high volume of data is flowing through the network, there is always network resource contention, leading to queuing delays, bottlenecks, packet drops, and network congestion. To account for finite bandwidth, build the system using lightweight data formats for the data in transit that will preserve the network bandwidth and avoid network congestion.
    无限带宽。第三条谬误是假设“带宽是无限的”。当大量数据流经网络时，总会出现网络资源争用，导致排队延迟、瓶颈、丢包和网络拥塞。为应对有限带宽，构建系统时应对在途数据采用轻量数据格式，以节省网络带宽、避免网络拥塞。
  • Secure network. The fourth fallacy is assuming that “the network is secure.” Assuming a network is always secure when there are multiple ways it can be compromised (including software bugs, OS vulnerabilities, viruses and malware, cross-site scripting, unencrypted communication, malicious middle actors, etc.) can lead to system compromise and failure. To account for insecure networks, build systems with a security-first mindset and perform defense testing and threat modeling on the built system.
    安全的网络。第四条谬误是假设“网络是安全的”。网络有多种被攻破的途径（包括软件缺陷、操作系统漏洞、病毒和恶意软件、跨站脚本、未加密通信、恶意中间人等），却假设它总是安全的，会导致系统被攻破和故障。为应对不安全的网络，应以安全优先的心态构建系统，并对建好的系统做防御测试和威胁建模。
  • Fixed topology. The fifth fallacy is assuming that “topology doesn’t change.” In distributed systems, the topology changes continuously because of node failures or node additions. Building a system that assumes a fixed topology will lead to system issues and failures due to latency and bandwidth constraints. Hence, the underlying topology must be abstracted out, and the system must be built oblivious to the underlying topology and tolerant to its changes.
    固定的拓扑。第五条谬误是假设“拓扑不会改变”。在分布式系统中，由于节点故障或节点加入，拓扑一直在变化。构建一个假设拓扑固定的系统，会因延迟和带宽约束而导致系统问题和故障。因此，底层拓扑必须被抽象出来，系统必须构建得对底层拓扑无感知、并能容忍其变化。
  • Single administrator. The sixth fallacy is assuming that “there is one administrator.” This can be a fair assumption in a very small system like a personal project, but this assumption breaks down in large-scale distributed computing, where multiple systems have separate OS, separate teams working on them, and thus, multiple administrators. To account for this, the system should be built in a decoupled manner, ensuring that repair and troubleshooting become easy and distributed, too.
    单一管理员。第六条谬误是假设“只有一个管理员”。在像个人项目这样非常小的系统中，这可能是个合理的假设，但在大规模分布式计算中这个假设就站不住脚了——那里多个系统有各自的操作系统、各自的团队，因而有多个管理员。为应对这一点，系统应以解耦的方式构建，确保修复和排障也变得容易、且可分布式进行。
  • Zero transport cost. The seventh fallacy is assuming that “transport cost is zero.” Network infrastructure has costs, including the costs of network servers, switches, routers, other hardware, the OS of that hardware, and the team cost to keep it all running smoothly. Thus, the assumption that the cost of transporting data from one node to another is negligible is false and must consequently be noted in budgets to avoid vast shortfalls.
    零传输成本。第七条谬误是假设“传输成本为零”。网络基础设施是有成本的，包括网络服务器、交换机、路由器、其他硬件的成本，这些硬件的操作系统，以及让这一切平稳运行的团队成本。因此，认为把数据从一个节点传到另一个节点的成本可以忽略不计，这种假设是错误的，必须在预算中记上这笔账，以免出现巨大缺口。
Page 47
  • Homogeneous network. The eighth fallacy is assuming that “the network is homogeneous.” A network is built with multiple devices with different configurations and using multiple protocols at different layers. Taking into consideration the heterogeneity of the network as well as focusing on the interoperability of the system (i.e., ensuring that subsystems can communicate and work together despite having such differences) will help to avoid this pitfall.
    同质的网络。第八条谬误是假设“网络是同质的”。一个网络由多台配置不同的设备构成，并在不同层次使用多种协议。考虑到网络的异构性、同时关注系统的互操作性（即确保各子系统尽管存在这些差异仍能相互通信、协同工作），将有助于避开这个陷阱。
The AWS Well-Architected Framework consists of six core pillars that provide guidance and best practices for designing and building systems on the AWS cloud to avoid these fallacies and pitfalls. The Operational Excellence pillar avoids the fallacy of single administrator and homogeneous network. The Security pillar avoids the secure-network fallacy. The Reliability pillar avoids the fallacy of a reliable network and fixed topology. The Performance Efficiency pillar avoids the fallacy of zero latency and infinite bandwidth. The Cost Optimization and Sustainability pillars avoid the fallacy of zero transport cost. We won’t cover the Well-Architected Framework in detail here.
AWS 良好架构框架（Well-Architected Framework）包含六大核心支柱，为在 AWS 云上设计和构建系统、避开这些谬误和陷阱提供指导和最佳实践。卓越运营支柱避免单一管理员和同质网络的谬误；安全支柱避免网络安全的谬误；可靠性支柱避免可靠网络和固定拓扑的谬误；性能效率支柱避免零延迟和无限带宽的谬误；成本优化与可持续性支柱避免零传输成本的谬误。此处不展开讲解良好架构框架。

These fallacies cover the basic assumptions we should avoid when building large-scale systems. Overall, neglecting the fallacies of distributed computing can lead to a range of issues, including system failures, performance bottlenecks, data inconsistencies, security vulnerabilities, scalability challenges, and increased complexity of system administration. It is important to acknowledge and account for these fallacies during the design and implementation of distributed systems to ensure their robustness, reliability, and effective operation in real-world environments.

这些谬误涵盖了我们在构建大规模系统时应避免的基本假设。总体而言，忽视分布式计算谬误会导致一系列问题，包括系统故障、性能瓶颈、数据不一致、安全漏洞、可扩展性挑战以及系统管理复杂度上升。在设计和实现分布式系统时，必须承认并考虑这些谬误，以确保它们在真实环境中健壮、可靠、有效地运行。

Now, let’s go through the trade-offs that are generally encountered when designing large-scale software systems.

现在，我们来过一下设计大规模软件系统时通常会遇到的各种取舍。

System Design Trade-offs

Page 48

System design involves making a number of trade-offs that can have a significant impact on the performance and usability of a system. When designing a system, you must consider factors like cost, scalability, reliability, maintainability, and robustness. These factors must be balanced to create a system that is optimized for the particular needs of the user. Ultimately, the goal is to create a system that meets user needs without sacrificing any of these important factors.

系统设计涉及做出一系列取舍，这些取舍会显著影响系统的性能和可用性。设计系统时，你必须考虑成本、可扩展性、可靠性、可维护性和健壮性等因素。这些因素必须相互平衡，才能创造出为用户特定需求而优化的系统。归根结底，目标是创造一个既满足用户需求、又不牺牲任何这些重要因素的系统。

For example, if a system needs to be highly reliable but also have scalability, then you need to consider the trade-offs between cost and robustness. A system with a high level of reliability may require more expensive components, but these components may also be robust and allow for scalability in the future. On the other hand, if cost is a priority, then you may have to sacrifice robustness or scalability to keep the system within budget.

例如，如果一个系统既要高可靠又要有可扩展性，那么你就需要考虑成本与健壮性之间的取舍。一个高可靠的系统可能需要更昂贵的组件，但这些组件可能也很健壮，并允许未来扩展。另一方面，如果成本是优先项，那么你可能不得不牺牲健壮性或可扩展性，以使系统控制在预算内。

Trade-offs in addition to cost and scalability must be taken into account when designing a system. Performance, security, maintainability, and usability are all important considerations that must be weighed. In this section, we will discuss some theoretical trade-offs that arise in system design.

设计系统时，除了成本和可扩展性，还必须考虑其他取舍。性能、安全、可维护性和可用性都是必须权衡的重要考量。本节我们讨论系统设计中出现的一些理论上的取舍。

Time Versus Space

Time-space trade-offs or time-memory trade-offs arise inherently in implementing algorithms in computer science for the workload, even in distributed systems. These trade-offs are necessary because system designers need to consider the time limitations of the algorithms and sometimes use extra memory or storage to make sure everything works optimally. One example of such a trade-off is using look-up tables in memory or data storage instead of performing recalculations and thus serving more requests by just looking up precomputed values.

在计算机科学中为工作负载实现算法时（即使在分布式系统中），时空取舍或时间-内存取舍会天然出现。这些取舍是必要的，因为系统设计者需要考虑算法的时间限制，有时会用额外的内存或存储来确保一切最优运行。这种取舍的一个例子是在内存或数据存储中使用查找表，而不是重新计算，从而只需查表读取预计算值就能服务更多请求。

Latency Versus Throughput

Another trade-off that arises inherently in system design is latency versus throughput. Before diving into the trade-off, let’s make sure you understand these concepts.

系统设计中天然出现的另一对取舍是延迟与吞吐量。在深入这对取舍之前，我们先确保你理解这些概念。

Page 49

Latency, processing time, and response time. Latency is the time that a request waits to be handled. Processing time, on the other hand, is the time taken by the system to process the request once it is picked up. Hence, the overall response time is the duration between the request that was sent and the corresponding response that was received, accounting for network and server latencies. Mathematically, it can be represented by the following formula:

延迟、处理时间和响应时间。延迟是请求等待被处理的时间。而处理时间是系统一旦拿到请求后处理它所花的时间。因此，整体响应时间是从发出请求到收到对应响应之间的时长，其中计入了网络和服务器延迟。在数学上可由下式表示：

Response Time = Latency + Processing Time

Throughput and bandwidth. Throughput and bandwidth are metrics of network data capacity and are used to account for network scalability and load. Bandwidth refers to the maximum amount of data that could theoretically travel from one point in the network to another in a given time. Throughput refers to the actual amount of data transmitted and processed throughout the network. Thus, bandwidth describes the theoretical limit, and throughput provides the empirical metric. The throughput is always lower than the bandwidth unless the network is operating at its maximum efficiency. Bandwidth is a limited resource because each network device can handle and process only a limited capacity of data before passing it to the next network device, and some devices consume more bandwidth than others. Insufficient bandwidth can lead to network congestion, which slows connectivity.

吞吐量和带宽。吞吐量和带宽是衡量网络数据容量的指标，用于考量网络的可扩展性和负载。带宽指在给定时间内，理论上能从网络中一点传输到另一点的最大数据量。吞吐量指整个网络中实际传输和处理的数据量。因此，带宽描述理论上限，吞吐量提供实测指标。除非网络运行在最高效率，否则吞吐量总是低于带宽。带宽是有限资源，因为每台网络设备在把数据传给下一台网络设备之前，只能处理和转发有限容量的数据，而且有些设备比其他设备消耗更多带宽。带宽不足会导致网络拥塞，从而拖慢连接。

Since latency measures how long the packets take to reach the destination in a network, while throughput measures how many packets are processed within a specified period of time, they have an inverse relationship. Higher latency causes packets to queue up in the network, slowing packet processing and ultimately reducing throughput.

由于延迟衡量的是网络中数据包到达目的地所花的时间，而吞吐量衡量的是在指定时间段内处理了多少个数据包，二者呈反比关系。更高的延迟会导致数据包在网络中排队，拖慢数据包处理，最终降低吞吐量。

Because the system is being gauged for lower latency under high throughput or load, the metric to capture latency is through percentiles, such as p50, p90, p99, and so on. For example, the p90 latency is the highest latency value (slowest response) of the fastest 90% of requests. In other words, 90% of requests have responses that are equal to or faster than the p90 latency value. Note that average latency of a workload is not used as a metric because averages as point estimates are susceptible to outliers. Because of the latency versus throughput trade-off, the latency will also increase as the load is increased on the system for higher throughput. Hence, systems should be designed with an aim for maximal throughput within acceptable latency.

由于衡量的是系统在高吞吐量或高负载下的更低延迟，捕捉延迟的指标用的是百分位数，例如 p50、p90、p99 等等。例如，p90 延迟是最快的那 90% 请求中最高的延迟值（最慢的响应）。换句话说，90% 的请求其响应等于或快于 p90 延迟值。注意，工作负载的平均延迟不用作指标，因为平均值作为点估计容易受离群值影响。由于延迟与吞吐量的取舍，当为更高吞吐量而加大系统负载时，延迟也会上升。因此，系统设计应着眼于在可接受延迟内实现最大吞吐量。

Performance Versus Scalability

As discussed in “Scalability” on page 20, scalability is the system’s ability to respond to increased demand and load. On the other hand, performance is how fast the system responds to a single request. A service is scalable if it results in increased performance in a manner proportional to resources added. When a system has performance problems, it is slow for a single user (p50 latency = 100 ms), but when the system has scalability problems, the system may be fast for some users (p50 latency = 1 ms for one hundred requests) but slow under heavy load for the users (p50 latency = 100 ms under one hundred thousand requests).

如第 20 页“可扩展性”一节所讨论的，可扩展性是系统响应增长的需求和负载的能力。而性能是系统响应单个请求有多快。如果一个服务性能的提升与所加入资源成正比，那它就是可扩展的。当系统有性能问题时，它对单个用户就慢（p50 延迟 = 100 毫秒）；而当系统有可扩展性问题时，它对某些用户可能很快（100 个请求时 p50 延迟 = 1 毫秒），但在高负载下对用户变慢（10 万个请求时 p50 延迟 = 100 毫秒）。

Consistency Versus Availability

Strong consistency in data storage and retrieval is the guarantee that every read receives the most recent write, while high availability is the requirement of the system to always provide a nonerror response to the request. In a distributed system where the network fails (i.e., packets get dropped or delayed due to the fallacies of distributed computing leading to partitions), there emerges an inherent trade-off between strong consistency and high availability. This trade-off is called the CAP theorem, also known as Brewer’s theorem.

数据存储与检索中的强一致性，保证每次读都收到最近一次写；而高可用性要求系统总是对请求返回非错误响应。在一个网络发生故障的分布式系统中（即由于分布式计算谬误导致丢包或延迟、进而形成分区），强一致性与高可用性之间就出现了固有的取舍。这一取舍称为 CAP 定理，也称 Brewer 定理。

Page 50

CAP theorem. The CAP theorem, illustrated as a Venn diagram in Figure 1-7, states that it is impossible for a distributed system to simultaneously provide all three of the following guarantees: consistency (C), availability (A), and partition tolerance (P). According to the theorem, a distributed system can provide at most two of these guarantees at any given time. Systems need to be designed to handle network partitions because networks aren’t reliable, and hence, partition tolerance needs to be built in. So the CAP theorem implies that in the presence of a network partition, one has to choose between consistency and availability.

CAP 定理。CAP 定理用韦恩图示于图 1-7，它指出：一个分布式系统不可能同时提供以下三项保证中的全部三项：一致性（C）、可用性（A）和分区容忍（P）。根据该定理，分布式系统在任一时刻最多只能提供其中两项保证。系统需要被设计为能处理网络分区，因为网络并不可靠，因此必须内建分区容忍。所以 CAP 定理意味着，在出现网络分区时，必须在一致性和可用性之间做出选择。

However, the CAP theorem is frequently misunderstood to mean that one has to choose to abandon one of the three guarantees at all times. In fact, the choice is really between consistency and availability only when a network partition or failure happens; at all other times, the trade-off has to be made based on the PACELC theorem.

然而，CAP 定理常被误解为：人必须在任何时候都选择放弃三项保证之一。事实上，只有当网络分区或故障发生时，才真正需要在一致性和可用性之间做选择；在其他所有时候，取舍都要基于 PACELC 定理来做。

PACELC theorem. The PACELC theorem, illustrated as a decision flowchart in Figure 1-8, is a more nuanced version of the CAP theorem. It states that in the case of network partitioning (P) in a distributed computer system, one must choose between availability (A) and consistency (C) as per the CAP theorem, but otherwise (E), even when the system is running normally in the absence of partitions, one has to choose between latency (L) and consistency (C). This trade-off arises naturally because to handle network partitions, data and services are replicated in large-scale systems, leading to the choice between the consistency spectrum and the corresponding latency.

PACELC 定理。PACELC 定理用决策流程图示于图 1-8，是 CAP 定理更细致的版本。它指出：在分布式计算机系统发生网络分区（P）时，必须按 CAP 定理在可用性（A）和一致性（C）之间选择；但在其他时候（E），即使系统在没有分区的情况下正常运行，也必须在延迟（L）和一致性（C）之间选择。这一取舍是自然出现的，因为为了处理网络分区，大规模系统中会复制数据和服务，从而导致在一致性谱系与相应延迟之间做出选择。

Page 51

If the system tries to provide for strong consistency at one end of the consistency spectrum model, it has to do replication with synchronous communication and blocking to ensure that all the read replicas receive the most recent write, waiting on the acknowledgment from all the replica nodes, which adds to high latency. On the other hand, if the system does asynchronous replication without waiting for acknowledgment from all nodes, it will end up providing eventual consistency (i.e., the read request will eventually reflect the last recent write) when the replica node has acknowledged the data mutation change for serving the requests.

如果系统试图在一致性谱系模型的一端提供强一致性，它就必须用同步通信和阻塞来做复制，以确保所有读副本都收到最近一次写，并等待所有副本节点的确认，这就带来了高延迟。另一方面，如果系统做异步复制、不等待所有节点确认，那么当副本节点确认了数据变更后再服务请求时，最终提供的就是最终一致性（即读请求最终会反映最近一次写）。

The CAP and PACELC theorems are important concepts in distributed systems design that provide a framework for understanding the trade-offs involved in designing highly available and strongly consistent systems.

CAP 定理和 PACELC 定理是分布式系统设计中的重要概念，它们为理解设计高可用、强一致系统时涉及的取舍提供了框架。

We will cover how nonrelational stores navigate the CAP theorem trade-off by discussing BASE properties in detail in Chapter 3.
我们将在第 3 章通过详细讨论 BASE 性质，讲解非关系存储如何应对 CAP 定理的取舍。

Given such requirements, fallacies, and trade-offs in system design, to avoid repeating mistakes of the past, we should adhere to a set of guidelines that the previous generation of software design practitioners learned. Let’s dig into those now.

鉴于系统设计中有这些需求、谬误和取舍，为避免重蹈覆辙，我们应当遵循上一代软件设计实践者总结出的一套准则。下面我们就来深入这些准则。

Page 52

System Design Guidelines

System design will always present the most interesting and challenging trade-offs, and a system designer should be aware of the hidden costs and be well equipped to get it right—though not perfect! These guidelines, which have emerged over years of practicing system design, help us avoid pitfalls and handle trade-offs when designing large-scale systems. These guidelines aren’t just vague generalities but rather virtues that help us reflect on why the system was designed and implemented the way it was and why that was the right thing to do.

系统设计总是会呈现出最有趣、也最具挑战性的取舍，系统设计者应当意识到隐性成本，并做好准备把事情做对——尽管不必完美！这些准则来自多年系统设计实践，帮助我们在设计大规模系统时避开陷阱、处理取舍。这些准则不只是模糊的泛泛之谈，而是一些美德，帮助我们反思：系统为何被这样设计和实现、以及为何这样做是正确的。

Guideline of Isolation: Build It Modularly

“Controlling complexity is the essence of computer programming.” — Brian Kernighan

The first guideline is to build the system modularly—that is, break a complex system down into smaller, independent components or modules that can function independently yet also work together to form the larger system. Building a large-scale system modularly helps improve all its requirements:

第一条准则是模块化地构建系统——也就是把一个复杂系统拆成更小的、独立的组件或模块，它们既能独立运行、又能协同组成更大的系统。模块化地构建大规模系统有助于改善它的各项要求：

  • Maintainability. Modules can be updated or replaced individually without affecting the rest of the system.
    可维护性。模块可以单独更新或替换，而不影响系统的其他部分。
  • Reusability. Modules can be reused in different systems or projects, reducing the amount of new development required.
    可复用性。模块可以在不同系统或项目中复用，减少所需的新开发量。
  • Scalability. Modules can be added or removed and even scaled independently as needed to accommodate changes in requirements or to support growth.
    可扩展性。模块可以按需增减，甚至独立伸缩，以适应需求变化或支持增长。
  • Reliability. Modules can be tested and validated independently, reducing the risk of system-wide failures.
    可靠性。模块可以独立测试和验证，降低系统级故障的风险。

Modular systems can be implemented in a variety of ways, including through the use of microservice architecture, component-based development, and modular programming, which we will cover in more detail in Chapter 7. However, designing modular systems can be challenging as it requires careful consideration of the interfaces between modules, data sharing and flow, and dependencies.

模块化系统可以通过多种方式实现，包括使用微服务架构、基于组件的开发和模块化编程，我们将在第 7 章更详细地讲解。然而，设计模块化系统可能颇具挑战，因为它需要仔细考虑模块之间的接口、数据共享与流动以及依赖关系。

Page 53

Guideline of Simplicity: Keep It Simple, Silly

“Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.” — attributed to Albert Einstein

The second guideline is to keep the design simple by avoiding complex and unnecessary features and overengineering. To build simple systems using the KISS (Keep It Simple, Silly) guideline, designers can follow these principles:

第二条准则是通过避免复杂、不必要的功能和过度设计来保持设计简单。要用 KISS（Keep It Simple, Silly，保持简单，傻瓜式）准则构建简单系统，设计者可以遵循以下原则：

  • Identify the core requirements. Determine the essential features and functions the system must have and prioritize them.
    识别核心需求。确定系统必须具备的核心功能和特性，并排定优先级。
  • Minimize the number of components. Reduce the number of components or modules in the system, making sure each component serves a specific purpose.
    尽量减少组件数量。减少系统中组件或模块的数量，确保每个组件都有明确用途。
  • Avoid overengineering. Don’t add unnecessary complexity to the system, such as features that are not necessary for its functioning.
    避免过度工程。不要给系统增加不必要的复杂度，例如对其运行并非必需的功能。
  • Make the system easy to use. Ensure that the system is intuitive and straightforward for users to use and understand.
    让系统易于使用。确保系统直观、对用户来说容易使用和理解。
  • Test and refine. Test the system to ensure that it works as intended, and make changes to simplify the system if necessary.
    测试并改进。测试系统以确保它按预期工作，并在必要时做出改动来简化系统。

By following the KISS guideline, you as a system designer can build simple, efficient, and effective systems that are easier to maintain and less prone to failure.

通过遵循 KISS 准则，作为系统设计者的你可以构建简单、高效、有效的系统，它们更易维护、更不容易出故障。

Guideline of Performance: Metrics Don’t Lie

“Performance problems cannot be solved only through the use of Zen meditation.” — Jeffrey C. Mogul

The third guideline is to measure, then build, and rely on the metrics since you can’t cheat the performance and scalability. Metrics and observability are crucial for understanding the behavior and performance of large-scale systems and for identifying potential issues before they become problems.

第三条准则是先度量、再构建，并依赖指标，因为你骗不了性能和可扩展性。指标和可观测性对于理解大规模系统的行为和性能、以及在潜在问题变成真正问题之前发现它们，至关重要。

Page 54

Metrics are quantitative measures that are used to assess the performance of a system. They provide a way to track key performance indicators, such as resource utilization, response times, and error rates, and to identify trends and patterns in system behavior. By monitoring metrics, engineers can detect performance bottlenecks and anomalies and take corrective actions to improve the overall performance and reliability of the system.

指标是用于评估系统性能的定量度量。它们提供了一种跟踪关键性能指标（例如资源利用率、响应时间和错误率）、并识别系统行为趋势和模式的方式。通过监控指标，工程师可以发现性能瓶颈和异常，并采取纠正措施来提升系统的整体性能和可靠性。

Observability refers to the degree to which the state of a system can be inferred from its externally visible outputs. This includes being able to monitor system health and diagnose problems in real time. Observability is important in large-scale systems because it provides a way to monitor the behavior of complex systems and detect issues that may be affecting their performance.

可观测性指系统状态能够从其外部可见输出中被推断出来的程度。这包括能够实时监控系统健康状况、诊断问题。可观测性在大规模系统中很重要，因为它提供了一种监控复杂系统行为、发现可能影响其性能的问题的方式。

Together, metrics and observability provide the information needed to make informed decisions about the operation and management of large-scale systems. By ensuring that systems are properly instrumented with metrics and that observability is designed into the system, you can detect and resolve issues more quickly, prevent outages, and improve the system’s overall performance and reliability.

指标和可观测性合在一起，为大规模系统的运行和管理提供做出明智决策所需的信息。通过确保系统被恰当地埋点指标、并把可观测性设计进系统，你可以更快地发现和解决问题、预防宕机，并提升系统的整体性能和可靠性。

Guideline of Trade-offs: There Is No Such Thing as a Free Lunch

“Get it right. Neither abstraction nor simplicity is a substitute for getting it right.” — Butler Lampson

The fourth guideline is “there is no such thing as a free lunch” (TINSTAAFL), or the realization that all decisions come with trade-offs and that optimizing for one aspect of a system often comes at the expense of others. There are always trade-offs and compromises that must be made when designing a system. For example, choosing a highly optimized solution for a specific problem might result in reduced maintainability or increased complexity. Conversely, opting for a simple solution might result in lower performance or increased latency.

第四条准则是“天下没有免费的午餐”（TINSTAAFL），也就是认识到所有决策都伴随取舍，为系统某一方面做优化往往要以牺牲其他方面为代价。设计系统时总有必须做出的取舍和妥协。例如，为某个特定问题选择一个高度优化的方案，可能会降低可维护性或增加复杂度。反过来，选择一个简单方案，可能会导致性能降低或延迟增加。

The TINSTAAFL guideline highlights the need for careful consideration and balancing of competing factors in system design, such as performance, scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost. Designers must weigh the trade-offs between these factors and make informed decisions that meet the specific requirements and constraints of each project. Ultimately, you need to realize that there is no single solution that is optimal in all situations and that, to build the right system, you as the system designer must carefully consider the trade-offs and implications of your design decisions.

TINSTAAFL 准则强调，需要在系统设计中仔细权衡和平衡相互竞争的因素，例如性能、可扩展性、可靠性、可维护性和成本。设计者必须权衡这些因素之间的取舍，做出满足每个项目具体需求和约束的明智决策。归根结底，你需要认识到不存在一种在所有情况下都最优的单一方案；要构建正确的系统，作为系统设计者的你必须仔细考虑设计决策的取舍和影响。

Guideline of Use Cases: It Always Depends

“Not everything worth doing is worth doing well.” — Tom West
Page 55

The fifth guideline is design always depends because system design is a complex, multifaceted process that is influenced by a variety of factors, including requirements, user needs, technological constraints, cost, scalability, maintenance, and even regulations. By considering these and other factors, you can develop systems that meet the needs of the users, are feasible to implement, and are sustainable over time. Since there are many ways to design a system to solve a common problem, this guideline indicates a stronger underlying truth: there is no one “best” way to design the system. In other words, there is no silver bullet. Thus, we settle for something reasonable and hope it is good enough.

第五条准则是：设计永远取决于具体情况，因为系统设计是一个复杂、多层面的过程，受多种因素影响，包括需求、用户需要、技术约束、成本、可扩展性、维护、甚至法规。通过考虑这些以及其他因素，你可以开发出满足用户需求、可行实现、并能长期持续的系统。既然解决一个常见问题有许多种设计系统的方式，这条准则指向一个更强的底层事实：设计系统没有唯一的“最佳”方式。换句话说，没有银弹。因此，我们选择一个合理的方案，并希望它足够好。

Conclusion

This chapter has given you a solid introduction to how we design software systems. We’ve talked about the main concepts underlying system design, the trade-offs we must make when dealing with big software systems, the fallacies to avoid in building such large-scale systems, and smart guidelines for avoiding such fallacies.

本章为你扎实介绍了我们如何设计软件系统。我们谈到了系统设计背后的主要概念、处理大型软件系统时必须做出的取舍、构建这类大规模系统时要避免的谬误，以及避免这些谬误的聪明准则。

Think of system design as like balancing on a seesaw: you must find the right equilibrium between different trade-offs. As an overall guideline, system design is always a trade-off between competing factors, and you as a system designer must carefully weigh these factors to create systems that are effective and efficient.

可以把系统设计想象成在跷跷板上保持平衡：你必须在不同取舍之间找到恰当的平衡。作为一条总体准则，系统设计永远是在相互竞争的因素之间做取舍，作为系统设计者的你必须仔细权衡这些因素，才能创建出有效且高效的系统。

In the rest of Part I, we’re going to explore the basic building blocks of systems. We’ll talk about important topics like where we store data, how we speed things up with caches, how we distribute work with load balancers, and how different parts of a system talk to one another through networking and orchestration.

在第一部分的剩余章节中，我们将探索系统的基本积木。我们会讨论一些重要话题：数据存在哪里、如何用缓存提速、如何用负载均衡器分发工作，以及系统的不同部分如何通过网络和编排相互通信。

Once you’ve got a handle on those basics, we’ll dive into the world of AWS systems in Part II. This will help you understand how to make big and powerful systems using Amazon Web Services. All this knowledge will come together in Part III, where we’ll put everything into practice and learn how to design and build large-scale systems on AWS for specific use cases.

一旦你掌握了这些基础，我们将在第二部分深入 AWS 系统的世界。这会帮助你理解如何用 Amazon Web Services 构建大型而强大的系统。所有这些知识将在第三部分汇合，我们会把一切付诸实践，学习如何在 AWS 上针对特定用例设计和构建大规模系统。

Before we get there, our next stop is exploring different ways to store data and introducing you to relational databases.

在到达那一步之前，下一站是探索不同的数据存储方式，并向你介绍关系数据库。
